analysis:
Reviewed all three batch analyses and available replayed patches/metadata. No independently supported security regression was established. The replay is incomplete (15 of 27 source units omitted), so prior clean analyses do not establish clearance.

Bedrock workload admission cumulatively reserves scheduled calls plus one repair slot, caps native requests at 500, and makes ceiling exhaustion sticky (.github/scripts/threat_review/bedrock.py:46-88). Larger output and response-time allowances increase bounded paid exposure, but do not by themselves demonstrate a spending-control bypass. The entrypoint validates a 60–3000-second deadline and cancels its alarm during finalization (.github/scripts/threat-model-review.py:16-43). The runner rejects repeat run attempts before scanning, marks lifecycle failures finished, and explicitly labels incomplete terminal reports as requiring human review (.github/scripts/threat_review/budget_runner.py:38-48,175-177,225-228). These patches reconcile the earlier rerun question, but report wording alone does not prove merge-gate enforcement.

Remaining material questions: verify depth_policy.source_depth and Scanner.call/integrate preserve critical-source coverage, findings, uncertainty and convergence; reconcile every source/depth/integration/repair call with workload admission and fallback spending reservations; confirm the actual workflow deadline permits durable publication and that the clearance gate rejects incomplete or stale results. The actual workflow, scanner scheduling, diagnostic producers and gate implementations are not replayed sufficiently to independently resolve those cross-file contracts. Changelog and build-guide claims are not substitutes for enforcement.

The supplied changes concern CI review availability, cost and security-review integrity. They do not visibly alter provider plaintext custody, encryption, serving authorization, attestation, inference/cache isolation, payment-ledger operations or fan-helper authority under A-001, A-003, TB-002 and TB-011. The canonical index supplies no dedicated paid-CI boundary; increased allowances warrant checking the CI resource contract, not inventing a runtime threat or deployment assumption.
